clue.text: Suit for royal households following the latest fashion

parts.note: a monarch's household and retinue is a court, so royal households are courts
hip means trendy, up with the latest fashion

explanation.surface: A suit tailored for palace life in the newest style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, matching 'fashion', but here it is the old sense of wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit, in the old sense, is the wooing of a prospective partner.

clue.text: Supply food and a location, say, for this wailing noise

parts.note: to cater is to provide food

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a wall is a place where something is set or hung, a location

explanation.surface: Providing food and a venue leads to an awful howling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that WALL is taken by its sound, giving WAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's shrill yowling, or any loud discordant cry, is a wailing noise.

clue.text: Mostly refined oppidan

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: urbane means suave and refined

explanation.surface: A polished townsman, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppidan, from Latin oppidum, 'town', means of a town; it is also an Eton term for a non-scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidan means of a town, the same as relating to a city.

clue.text: In rags, but made lace to clothe queen

indicators.note: clothe means wrap around, so the lacemaking surrounds the queen

parts.note: to tat is to make lace by hand, so made lace is tatted
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A ragged figure, yet someone made lace to dress the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: TATTING is handmade knotted lace, so 'made lace' is tatted; the queen is clothed by it, as 'to clothe' signals. 'In rags' is an adjective phrase matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes torn and worn to shreds are rags.

clue.text: Support for rising storyteller following script

indicators.note: following means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a hand is a style of handwriting, a script

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a storyteller is one who tells stories, a liar

explanation.surface: Help for an author whose career takes off after a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the storyteller upwards, and 'following' sets that after the script. 'Support' is the definition, a rail on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail to hold on stairs is a support for the hand.

clue.text: Hors-d'oeuvre the French tucked into with relish

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the French word goes into the starter

parts.note: pate, meat paste, is served as a starter
la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A diner tucks into a French starter with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a pickle to go with the starter, but it is the definition in its sense of taste or liking; 'tucked into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Palate, the sense of taste, means relish or liking for flavours.

clue.text: Her mother may be employed making buttons

definitions.text: Her mother may be employed making buttons

parts.words: Her mother may be employed making buttons
parts.note: the iridescent shell lining called 'mother-of-' this gem is traditionally used for buttons, so the gem's 'mother' goes into buttons

explanation.surface: A woman's mother takes a job in a button factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, the shell lining in which this gem forms, is known as its mother and is cut into buttons.

clue.text: Naughty child's predicament

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster's sticky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little imp of this name, and a tricky fix or plight is also one.

clue.text: Love to make fuss over allotment

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A gardener dotes on making a fuss over the vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' looks like a vegetable plot, but here it is a share handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep devotion or worship is an intense love.

clue.text: Italian money covers launch of this volume

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the money holds the next letter

parts.note: the lira, plural lire, was Italy's currency

indicators.note: a launch is a start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Italian funds pay for the publication of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch of this' gives T, which 'covers' puts inside LIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of capacity measures volume.

clue.text: Asian superman crossing borders of Belize

indicators.note: the superman is laid across the letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a titan is a giant of a person, a superman

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A heroic Asian figure travels across the frontiers of the Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: A titan is a figure of superhuman strength. 'crossing' signals that the giant is laid across the frontier letters, which 'borders of' picks from the country name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tibet, in the Himalaya, is an Asian.

clue.text: Action of management finding hair unacceptable

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
out means not allowed, as in 'that idea is out'

explanation.surface: Bosses take action against a worker whose hairstyle breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: A lockout is when employers shut workers out of the workplace during a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting employees out of work to pressure them in a dispute is a tactic used by employers.

clue.text: Wash item of sportswear in sea water

indicators.note: an item of something is a part of it, so the answer is a run of letters lying inside the next words

explanation.surface: Rinsing a piece of kit in salt water after playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'sportsweaR IN SEa'; 'item of' points to letters lying inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something lightly in clean water is to swill it through.

clue.text: Talk about volunteers I put in to strike back

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so I goes inside what has been built
about means around, so the talk wraps round the volunteers

parts.note: to relate is to tell or narrate, to talk of something
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone talks about joining the volunteers as a way of hitting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' first wraps the talk round the volunteers, giving RETALATE; 'put in' then sets I among the letters. TA, the Territorial Army, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to hit back or take revenge for an attack.

clue.text: Active head learning elegiacs originally in Greek

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the Greek word

parts.note: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so Greek

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: A lively headmaster studies elegiac verse in the original Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes H, L and E from 'head learning elegiacs', and 'in' puts them inside ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty and physically energetic is active.

clue.text: On a trip, comes to rest in Scotland?

parts.note: a trip is a drug experience, so someone on one is high
lands means comes down and settles

explanation.surface: Touching down in Scotland at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' suggests travel, but means drugged. The question mark flags that the answer is a part of Scotland rather than the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountainous north of Scotland is a region of that country, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Box for a coffee-grinder?

explanation.surface: Is a box suitable to house a coffee-grinder?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is the verb to fight with fists; an old slang word for a fist fight is a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: To mill is old slang for to fight with the fists; a small grinding device for coffee beans is also one.

clue.text: Modern lady involved with unusual treat

indicators.note: involved means tangled and unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of both words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman mixed up with an odd delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with unusual' signals one mixing of the nine letters; 'Modern' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means of the present age, contemporary.

clue.text: Advance in vehicle carrying a table

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the vehicle holds the other letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A loan made in a car that is transporting a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' looks like furniture being carried, but it is the definition: a table of dates. 'carrying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A table of days and dates for the year is a list ordered by date.

clue.text: Traditional subsidy, it's said, for defence-work

parts.note: stock means standard, conventional

indicators.note: it's said means as spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: aid is financial help, a subsidy

explanation.surface: A customary grant is reportedly used for military fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' turns AID into its sound, written ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier of upright stakes is a defensive fortification.

clue.text: Short Greek word for "device"

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: logos is the Greek for 'word'

explanation.surface: An abbreviated Greek term that is used to mean a device.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek for 'word' is LOGOS; 'Short' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and design a device is an emblem or symbol, which is what a company's emblem is.

clue.text: Drill-master's return by No.1 tram

indicators.note: return means go back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: by is the multiplication sign X, which is the Roman numeral ten
number one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sergeant goes home on the first-numbered tram route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' in arithmetic is 'times', written as X, the Roman ten. 'return' turns TEN + I + TRAM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict disciplinarian, named after a 17th-century French drill officer, is a stern instructor of parade drill.

clue.text: Guard thrilled to be employed on trains

parts.note: sent is slang for excited, carried away
RY is short for railway, the trains

explanation.surface: A guard delighted to get a job on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' looks like a train guard, but it is a soldier on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier standing watch at a post is a guard.

clue.text: Redemption of a children's writer out east

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter leaves the name

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons for children

explanation.surface: A children's author's salvation in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur RANSOME, author of 'Swallows and Amazons', loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: Redemption, buying back a captive, is the payment that frees them.

clue.text: Turn-about of valet converted by church

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A manservant abruptly changes his beliefs after a church conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges 'of valet' into VOLTEFA, before the church; 'converted' also hints at a change of belief, which is what a volte-face is.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy is an about-turn.

clue.text: Official is binding

explanation.surface: Something formal is obligatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Valid means officially authorised, and also legally binding as a contract can be.

clue.text: Composed type found in this hunting-land

explanation.surface: Printer's type set in a game reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, a chase is the metal frame that holds set type; it is also an old word for unenclosed hunting ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers lock composed type into an iron frame of this name; open land kept for hunting deer is also so called.

clue.text: Honour accepted by artist in good colour

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Honour accepted by artist in good colour'. OM inside ARA gives AROMA, but no sense of 'good colour' defines it; the paper likely misprinted 'odour', which setterError cannot record for a definition.
annotationWithheld.clue: Honour accepted by artist in good colour

clue.text: Medicine reportedly associated with you and me

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: associated means linked, and you and me is us, so the phrase is linked us

explanation.surface: A drug said to be connected with the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals that 'linked us' said quickly gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing syrup taken for coughs is a medicine.

clue.text: It's hard, being involved in a deal!

definitions.text: It's hard, being involved in a deal!

parts.words: It's hard, being involved in a deal!
parts.note: the hardest natural gem, traded by dealers, and also a playing-card suit dealt out in a hand

explanation.surface: A complaint about how tough negotiating can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a sigh about business, but 'hard' is the gem's hardness and 'deal' is a hand of cards, where one suit bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hardest natural mineral, a precious stone, is also one of the four card suits dealt in a hand.

clue.text: Fairly good when not so like fine powder

explanation.surface: Something is reasonably good unless it resembles fine dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so dusty' is a British idiom meaning fairly good.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'not so ...' with this word means fairly good; covered in or resembling powder is the plain sense.

clue.text: Soldier of fortune shows compassion about near disaster

indicators.note: about means around, so the compassion surrounds the rest

parts.note: mercy is compassion shown to someone

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of near are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hired fighter takes pity when catastrophe looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' scrambles 'near' into ENAR and 'about' wraps the compassion round it; 'shows' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of fortune is a hired fighter who serves for pay.
